target_customer: Robotics and computer vision teams that need labeled training images and cannot afford annotation services or in-house data teams
problem: Robot vision models are blocked on labeled data. Human annotation is slow and costly. SBX offered to turn 25 customer camera images into 25,000 labeled synthetic images using simulation software.
business_model: Synthetic data generation service, priced per dataset (pricing not found)
product_category: Synthetic training data for computer vision and robotics

founders.name: Ian Dewancker
founders.background_notes: Applied research in computer vision, robotics and ML optimization per the YC page.

founders.name: Artem Avdacev
founders.background_notes: Worked on fraud and fake reviews at Yelp per the YC page.

founders.name: Joshua Kuntz
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; little other detail given.

competitors.name: Datagen
competitors.what: Synthetic data for computer vision models, emerged from stealth in March 2021
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the sources opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Generating realistic labeled images from 25 customer photos needed simulation, rendering and domain-gap handling. The founders had applied research backgrounds, but the stack was largely off-the-shelf simulation software.

defensibility.rationale: No proprietary data or lock-in is described. Well funded rivals and engine vendors served the same need.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action against SBX is documented. Datagen raised $18.5M at launch in March 2021, and Unity launched synthetic datasets in 2021 according to search results.

market_need_then: Annotation cost and speed were widely cited blockers for computer vision teams; press in 2021 and 2022 described rapid growth of the synthetic data market. No SBX-specific customer evidence was found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct claims of 10x faster and cheaper, and the 25 images in, 25,000 out pitch

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community evidence about the brand was found; the name is an opaque abbreviation.

outcome_analysis: SBX Robotics was a five person Toronto team that joined YC in Winter 2021 with a synthetic data service for robot vision. Public sources show only a roughly $125K to $130K YC-sized investment and a PitchBook status of out of business. No post-mortem, closure date or cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned. Funded competitors such as Datagen existed at the time.
notes: Company website sbxrobotics.com did not resolve from the research environment. The round amount rests on CB Insights (130K, date shown as 1 Jan 2021, likely a placeholder); PitchBook reports 125K. Outcome search found no cause of closure. Unity and other 2021 synthetic data vendors appeared in searches without usable dated sources, so they are not listed.
